To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the movement of follicular and GC B cells is influenced by their interactions with the extracellular matrix, that follicular dendritic cells (FDCs) influence the dynamics of GC B cells by tethering them to the FDC network, and that the movement of GC B cells in the GC is influenced by the expression of CXCR4 on GC B cells and CXCL12 on FDCs.

1) GC B-cell movement is influenced by the GC microenvironment; 2) GC B-cell motility increases with age; 3) GC B-cell division is influenced by cell position within the GC; and 4) GC B-cells move towards the follicular boundary, which is the location of the most rapidly proliferating B-cells.

(a) GC B-cell motility is highly heterogeneous; (b) GC B-cell movement is influenced by cell division, the GC reaction to antigen, and GC B-cell affinity for follicular dendritic cells; (c) GC B-cell migration and cell division are coordinated to maximize the chance of B cells to receive antigen and survive in GCs; and (d) GC B-cell affinity and division rates are linked to GC B-cell survival and differentiation.
